lesson.title: Build a technical file that demonstrates compliance
lesson.summary: Build an inspectable, current technical file linked to requirements.

prerequisites.reason: It must include meaningful test evidence.

blocks: A **technical file** is the documentation demonstrating compliance with the system requirements. Article 11 requires it before market placement or service and requires it to stay current. Give authorities and relevant assessment bodies clear, comprehensive information.
A brochure saying “tested and safe” is not equivalent evidence. Article 8 connects compliance to intended purpose, generally acknowledged state of the art and risk management.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 8, 11; Annex IV points 1–9

blocks: A **technical evidence index** connects Annex IV elements to the actual version and records. Include purpose, provider, system/software versions, interactions, hardware, interface, product form and instructions.

Explain development methods and any pretrained components, design logic and choices, architecture and computing resources, dataset provenance/preparation, oversight, predetermined changes, signed/dated test reports and security measures. An index makes these retrievable; it does not replace them.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 8, 11; Annex IV points 1–9

blocks: Also include monitoring, group performance and limitations, foreseeable risks, relevant inputs and oversight, metric appropriateness, the risk-management system and lifecycle changes.

Annex IV further includes applied Official Journal standards or alternative solutions, the conformity declaration, and the post-market evaluation plan. Standards are technical specifications; a declaration states conformity. Their procedures are later-course handoffs, not assumed complete because this index lists them.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 8, 11; Annex IV points 1–9

blocks: An **integrated product file** for Annex I Section A contains both Article 11 information and the sector-law information in one set. Article 8 also permits appropriate integration of testing, reporting and procedures to avoid duplication.

Small firms may provide Annex IV elements in a simplified manner using the Commission’s designated form if they choose that route. Verify the form’s availability and version before relying on it. Simplification does not mean omitting the required elements.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 8, 11; Annex IV points 1–9

blocks: Northbridge’s file should identify the actual ranking version and locate evidence supporting its specified recruitment purpose. A change to labels, inputs or operation may require an update.
If a signed test report describes a different version, mark the evidence gap. A well-formatted index does not establish that the referenced evidence exists or applies.

questions.prompt: Northbridge has only a brochure and proposes creating the technical documentation after launch. What is wrong?

options.blocks: Before supply/service and maintained up to date
options.reason: Article 11 makes this a prior and continuing requirement.

options.blocks: Only after the first authority complaint
options.reason: The prior requirement is not complaint-triggered.

options.blocks: Only if the brochure is poorly designed
options.reason: Presentation quality does not replace technical evidence.
